page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. The virtual machine delivers 16 dedicated vCPUs spanning 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. Cache hierarchy details include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512 Foundation, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES hardware acceleration.

Memory resources total 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance comes without local bundled disk storage, requiring network-attached block storage for operating system and application data volumes. Networking performance provides a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included by default. The configuration contains no dedicated hardware accelerators or GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier multi-threaded throughput alongside lower single-threaded metrics. The instance achieved an average multi-core stress-ng score of 13975.48 and a PassMark CPU score of 15380.43, alongside a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 67.97 GB/sec. Conversely, single-thread tests show lower efficiency, with stress-ng single-core reaching 1311.19 and single-threaded gzip compression at 22.76 GB/sec, placing in the bottom quartile. Memory bandwidth registered 88.67 GB/sec read and 45.93 GB/sec write on uncached 256 MB blocks, supporting balanced multi-core memory operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.c6.4xlarge offers a balanced resource allocation for compute workloads that distribute execution evenly across parallel vCPUs rather than relying on high clock-speed per core. The absence of local NVMe storage and discrete GPUs avoids superfluous overhead for non-storage-bound compute processes. Suitable workloads include parallel batch processing, multi-threaded CI/CD compilation, distributed web serving, microservices architectures, and intermediate data transformation pipelines.

It does not provide bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and network interfaces deliver a 5 Gbps baseline bandwidth. Benchmark testing indicates mid-tier multi-core execution, reflected by a Geekbench multi-core score of 7299.0, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression of 67.97 GB/sec, and 13.44 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-threaded processing reflects lower performance across compression and CPU stress tests. The instance is structured for distributed, parallelized tasks such as CI/CD build runners, scalable web servers, container clusters, and general batch compute workflows.
